newsitem.title: USA: Lott--must have major capital gains tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Lott--must have major capital gains tax cut.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Wednesday upcoming tax cut legislation must include "something dramatic" in capital gains tax relief such as a reduction in the top rate to 20 percent from 28 percent.

Lott, a Mississippi Republican, told reporters there were "some conflicting understandings" about what the budget deal worked out with the White House included on taxes. He did not confirm that the budget agreement would specify $35 billion of the tax cut should go for President Clinton's college education credits.
"We can't have too large a chunk of revenue changes go into that one area," Lott said when asked if the $35 billion tax credit for education was assured in the budget deal.

"We will have to have room for a capital gains tax rate cut to around 20 percent and the tax credit for families to $500," he said. These two taxes as well as a reduction in inheritance taxes are the Republicans top priorities.
